extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners and patent owners involved in inter partes review (IPR) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural timeline and statutory/regulatory requirements for filing, instituting, and concluding an Inter Partes Review (IPR) under the AIA and corresponding CFR provisions. Covers filing windows, content and service requirements, institution standards, response deadlines, and final-decision timing and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: Can be filed (1) 9 months after issue/reissue date or (2) after completion of post-grant review for any patent issued before, on, or after Sept. 16, 2012. AIA §6, but not more than a year after being served with a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing is constrained by both the 9-month post-issuance rule and the 1-year bar following service of a complaint; these timing rules derive from AIA §6. Check applicable issuance date and any service of complaint to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable likelihood standard for institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Has to establish “a reasonable likelihood that the requester would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the request.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive threshold the PTO (PTAB) uses to decide whether to institute an IPR. If the petition does not meet this standard, the IPR will not be instituted. (Cited source: 77 Fed. Reg. 48728 / codified at 37 C.F.R. § 42.108 and AIA §6.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete petition contents (fee and service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete petition must include filing fee and be served on patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing is insufficient without the required fee and proper service on the patent owner. See 77 Fed. Reg. 48728 (codified as 37 C.F.R. § 42.106) for details on payment and service requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional response has to be filed no more than 3 months after filing date of petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may file a preliminary response but must do so within the 3-month window after the petition filing date. See 77 Fed. Reg. 48728 (codified at 37 C.F.R. § 42.107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution decision timing and initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution to Inter Partes Review (no more than 6 months after petition) — only if reasonable likelihood standard is met. Inter Partes Review can proceed on all or some of the challenged claims. Initiated within 3 months of the preliminary response or the last day during which such a response could have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTAB must decide on institution within six months of petition filing, applying the reasonable-likelihood standard; if instituted, the decision whether to proceed on all or some claims is discretionary. The IPR is initiated within 3 months after the preliminary response period closes (either after the filing of a preliminary response or after the last day such a response could have been filed). Authorities: 77 Fed. Reg. 48728 (37 C.F.R. § 42.108) and AIA §6 (codifying 35 U.S.C. § 314(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response to instituted grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file response to the petition addressing any grounds not already denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner’s substantive response to instituted grounds is permitted; the due date is either as specified in the Board's order or three months after institution of post-grant review. See 77 Fed. Reg. 48728 (codified at 37 C.F.R. § 42.120).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final determination timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final determination no more than 1 year after initiation of post-grant review (Extendable by no more than 6 months for a good cause or more if joinder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPR must reach a final written decision within one year of institution, subject to limited extensions (up to 6 months for good cause and additional time where joinder applies). See 77 Fed. Reg. 48727 (codified at 37 C.F.R. § 42.100) for the timing and extension rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO limit on number of petitions / dismissal as untimely
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO is authorized to limit the number of petitions but does not expect to do so. Under the proposed rules filings for inter partes reviews that are beyond the limit are dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the PTO may set limits on petitions, if a filing exceeds such a limit under the proposed rules it would be dismissed as untimely. See 77 Fed. Reg. 48688 and 77 Fed. Reg. 48727 (codified at 37 C.F.R. § 42.102) for the limit and dismissal treatment.
